subject.title: fix: keep inbound metadata in runtime context

question: Should OpenClaw land this narrow before-user runtime-context handoff, or make the tail-carrier/cache-breakpoint design from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100272 the canonical fix for the same metadata/cache problem?
rationale: Both PRs address the same core inbound-metadata leak into user prompt text, but the later PR explicitly argues this branch's carrier placement preserves context without recovering the prefix-cache cost, so the final architecture needs maintainer direction rather than an automated repair.

options.title: Prefer the tail-carrier PR
options.body: Review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100272 as the canonical landing path and close or supersede this PR once that branch is accepted or merged.

options.title: Land this narrow handoff
options.body: Accept the smaller prompt-cleanliness fix here and track tail placement/cache-breakpoint anchoring as separate follow-up work.

options.title: Ask for a combined branch
options.body: Have the authors fold this PR's clean handoff tests into a single branch that also implements the cache-stable tail carrier.

recommendation.title: Prefer the tail-carrier PR
recommendation.body: Review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100272 as the canonical landing path and close or supersede this PR once that branch is accepted or merged.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the overlapping tail-carrier PR and supplied the placement analysis that now determines which branch should be canonical.
